stages.title: Choose
stages.body: Select the prompt whose terms, tension, thesis and examples can be controlled.

stages.title: Decode
stages.body: Define key terms in context and locate the hidden contrast or relationship.

stages.title: Thesis
stages.body: State a qualified arguable position by the end of the introduction.

stages.title: Plan
stages.body: Build distinct reason, mechanism, consequence, limitation and response moves.

stages.title: Introduction
stages.body: Enter the issue directly; avoid dictionary openings and decorative quotations.

stages.title: Paragraph architecture
stages.body: Use claim, explanation, safe example and explicit link to thesis.

stages.title: Coherence
stages.body: Order paragraphs so each advances rather than repeats the argument.

stages.title: Counterargument
stages.body: Present a genuine objection or limit and answer or accommodate it.

stages.title: Evidence discipline
stages.body: Use defensible illustrations and never invent statistics or quotations.

stages.title: Style
stages.body: Prefer plain formal English, controlled sentence length and precise connectors.

stages.title: Word and time control
stages.body: Target about 600 words and reserve a final revision window.

stages.title: Revision and verdict
stages.body: Check thesis, paragraph jobs, grammar, unsupported claims, count and conclusion.
